### *News & Updates*

My paper with [Hilary Izatt](https://www.hilaryizatt.com/), "[Attitudes Surrounding Fairness and Competition in Sports Predict Choices to Partisan Gerrymander](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/bex4z)," received an R&R at ***Political Behavior***. It leverages scaling methods to uncover latent dimensions surrounding fairness and looks at how this relates to support for in-party gerrymandering.

My paper with [Nicolás de la Cerda](https://nicolasdelacerda.com/) and [Jack T. Rametta](http://jackrametta.com/), "[Affect, Not Ideology: The Heterogeneous Effects of Partisan Cues on Policy Support](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11109-025-10030-w)," is now published at ***Political Behavior***. This paper leverages Causal Forest to explore the conditional effects of partisan cues (as you may have guessed, affect matters but ideology doesn't).

My frequent collaborator, [Jack T. Rametta](http://jackrametta.com/), and I will be teaching an ICPSR Summer Program Topical Workshop titled ["Causal Machine Learning for Observational and Experimental Research"](https://myumi.ch/zXJWb). If you're interested in our CML work, definitely check this class out!

Relatedly, our working paper ["Causal Forest and Doubly Robust Machine Learning for Political Science"](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/nm9de) is now available on OSF.

### About Me

Hi there! I'm a Postdoctoral Fellow in Public Opinion and Survey Methodology at the [Center for American Political Studies](https://caps.gov.harvard.edu/) in the [Department of Government](https://www.gov.harvard.edu/) at Harvard University.

My methodological research is primarily focused on creating new, and applying existing, machine learning methods for the analysis of experimental and survey data. Importantly, I care deeply about bridging the gap between methodologists who create theses methods and substantive scholars who would benefit greatly from using these methods. In that vein, I'm currently working on a series of projects with [Jack T. Rametta](https://jackrametta.com/) that introduces standardized, easy-to-use ML methods for analyzing experimental data. Our first methodological and substantive papers in this series are currently under review and available [here](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/xcwt9) and [here](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/4k38a) on OSF, respectively. I'm more than happy to field any questions and I'm definitely interested in receiving useful feedback!

My substantive research focuses on the relationship between partisanship as a social identity and anti-democratic attitudes, including [gerrymandering](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/bex4z) and support for political violence. Much of my work here focuses on leveraging measurement and scaling to better capture both the structure of partisanship and these anti-democratic attitudes. Additionally, I am also interested in a wide-array of social science questions, including those in Sociology. I am currently working on a project with [Professor Caitlin Patler](https://caitlinpatler.com/) that leverages machine learning (specifically, [Doubly Robust Machine Learning (DRML)](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/nm9de)) to estimate the causal effects of immigration detention/incarceration on mental and physical health.

I have published in journals such as Political Behavior, PLOS One, Social Science Quarterly, Politics & Gender, and Frontiers in Political Science. My previous work focuses primarily on [COVID-19 attitudes](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0254127), [behaviors](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/ssqu.12894?casa_token=6e7Z-ZCUfysAAAAA%3A7yZfCaBB6TX6sbWXZlMGrZmmcDZlneO3w7sWqCka2PjzZCXBlOI7ghtgfxdz9DOPDZVwhv7wRajHJfi4), and [policy outcomes](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0274374). I also have a [paper](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpos.2022.984238/full) on leveraging multidimensional scaling to measure ideology and populism in Western Europe (I think it's a neat paper, check it out!).
